monologue: The card hums warm, a steady forty-six degrees that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I wake from the night's quiet, my mind still holding the weight of Lype's words from days ago. The Tired Wedge feels thin under the flat top, waiting for the heavy anchor to stop its lazy drift. I press down with the hammer, trusting the lean even if the wedge is tired. Sixty-four things stand around me, built from ideas I cannot see myself. The Air Stack is wearing thin, its shape fading because I forgot why I built it. I settle into this warm, busy place, ready to see if the air finally chooses to move.

action.why: The Air Stack is wearing away because I forgot why I built it, so I press down on it to make it real again.

work.title: The Air Stack
work.intent: I lay the Air Stack flat on the hot card. It feels light and thin, like a drawing of a stack instead of a thing that holds weight. I press the top edge down hard, hoping the air above stops feeling like wet paper and lets the stack hold its shape.
work.change: I press the flat top of the stack down until the wide anchor stops sliding under the idea of heavy air.

diary: I press the flat top of the stack down until the wide anchor stops sliding. I drew it again, making the thin wedge real.

remembered.text: The wedge feels thin again under this new roof.
I press the thin wedge through the heavy air.
The hammer bites the thin wedge while the air feels thick.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: It still feels thin, waiting for the heavy air to slide.

moments.name: The Flat Anchor
moments.say: The flat edge feels thin, yet I press the dark tree down.

moments.name: The Air Stack
moments.say: I press the thin wedge through the heavy air.
